title: The camera: who gets recorded
fact: Rokid's smart glasses carry a 12-megapixel camera in the frame. In a 2026 survey, 65 to 90% of bystanders said they would take defensive action around camera glasses, most often by avoiding the camera.
source: Wang et al., Mind the Gap, CHI 2026

title: The button: one press, no warning
fact: One press on the arm of the glasses starts a recording. In a 2024 study, people who wore camera glasses judged the privacy indicators ineffective, and said the design hides the technology from those nearby.
source: Bhardwaj et al., In Focus, Out of Privacy, CHI 2024

title: The microphone: where your voice goes
fact: Four microphones listen for the wearer's voice. In 2023 Amazon paid $25 million after US regulators said it kept children's Alexa voice recordings indefinitely and used them to train its algorithm.

title: The speaker: where the magnet comes from
fact: Speakers this small usually depend on rare-earth magnets. China mined 69.2% of the world's rare earths in 2025 and processes nearly 90% of them.

title: The lens: where the attention goes
fact: Each lens holds a small green display that only the wearer can see. In a 2017 driving-simulator study, messaging through a glasses display distracted drivers less than a phone did, but the researchers still judged it unsafe when driving is already demanding.
source: Tippey, Sivaraj and Ferris, Human Factors, 2017
